1.title: Physical Installations
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Physical Installations. It covers the exam area two point zero Network Implementation. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. two point four Explain important factors of physical installations: locations (I D F, M D F), rack size, port-side exhaust and intake, cabling (patch panel, fiber distribution panel), lockable racks. Power (U P S, P D U, power load, voltage). Environmental factors (humidity, fire suppression, temperature). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: two point zero Network Implementation (twenty percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: Locations
1.text: Locations. The figure shows this: An M D F connected to I D Fs on several floors.

1.title: Locations, continued
1.text: Locations. M D F (main distribution frame). The central wiring room where the provider connects and core equipment sits. I D F (intermediate distribution frame). A wiring closet on a floor or area that connects end devices and links back to the M D F.

1.title: Racks and cabling
1.text: Racks and cabling. Rack size. nineteen-inch wide standard rack; height in rack units (U), where one U equals one point seven five inches; common racks are forty-two U. Port-side exhaust or intake. Airflow direction of a device: mount it so intake faces the cold aisle and exhaust faces the hot aisle, or it recirculates hot air and overheats. Patch panel. Permanent cabling terminates at the panel; short patch cords link it to switches, which keeps cabling tidy and easy to change. Fiber distribution panel. The patch panel for fiber. Lockable racks. Physical security against tampering and unauthorized access. Exam tip: Intake faces the cold aisle; exhaust faces the hot aisle. A switch mounted backwards (port-side exhaust in a cold aisle) overheats.

1.title: Power
1.text: Power. U P S (uninterruptible power supply). Battery backup that keeps equipment running during short outages and cleans the power while a generator starts. P D U (power distribution unit). Distributes power to the devices in a rack; metered or switched models report load and let you power-cycle outlets remotely. Power load. The total power the devices draw; do not exceed circuit or U P S capacity. Voltage. Use the voltage the equipment needs (for example one hundred twenty V or two hundred eight or two hundred forty V).

1.title: Environmental factors
1.text: Environmental factors. Temperature. Keep within the manufacturer's range (cool, steady); hot aisle or cold aisle layout. Humidity. Not too dry (static electricity) and not too damp (corrosion, condensation). Fire suppression. Clean-agent gas or pre-action systems in server rooms; water sprinklers can destroy equipment. Exam tip: U P S equals battery; P D U equals power distribution in the rack; M D F equals main room; I D F equals floor closet. Exam tip: Intake faces the cold aisle and exhaust faces the hot aisle. A backwards switch overheats.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Equipment in a rack must keep running for a few minutes during a power outage. Which device fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: An uninterruptible power supply. A U P S provides battery backup.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which room is where the service provider connects and core equipment is typically located? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The main distribution frame. The M D F is the central wiring room.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A newly mounted switch overheats because its exhaust faces the cold aisle. What should be corrected? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: The airflow direction, so intake faces the cold aisle. Port-side exhaust and intake must match the aisle layout.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. An administrator wants to power-cycle a hung device in a remote rack. Which device helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A switched or managed P D U. Switched P D Us let you cycle outlets remotely.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which fire suppression method is preferred in a server room? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A clean-agent gas system. Clean agents suppress fire without damaging electronics.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. How tall is a two U device? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: three point five inches. One rack unit is one point seven five inches, so two U is three point five inches.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is an I D F? Answer: A wiring closet connecting end devices on a floor or area. Question two. What does a P D U do? Answer: Distributes power to the devices in a rack. Question three. What is a rack unit? Answer: one point seven five inches of vertical rack space.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which aisle should equipment intake face? Answer: The cold aisle. Question five. Name two environmental factors. Answer: For example temperature and humidity (and fire suppression). Question six. What does a patch panel do? Answer: Terminates permanent cabling so short patch cords link devices.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Locations: M D F (main room), I D F (floor closet). Racks: nineteen inch, units of one point seven five in, intake cold aisle, exhaust hot aisle, patch and fiber panels, lockable. Power: U P S (battery), P D U (distribution), load, voltage. Environment: temperature, humidity, clean-agent fire suppression.
